claim: Phosphorylation of serine 51 of the α subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (eIF2α) strongly influences protein folding homeostasis (proteostasis).
source: Protein folding homeostasis (proteostasis) is achieved by balancing the rate of production, folding and protein degradation. Proteostasis is strongly influenced by the phosphorylation state of serine 51 of the α subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (eIF2α) (Sonenberg and Hinnebusch, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sonenberg and Hinnebusch, 2009, indicating prior published work.

claim: Diverse stress conditions activate kinases that phosphorylate eIF2α, resulting in attenuated rates of translation initiation of most mRNAs.
source: Diverse stress conditions activate kinases that phosphorylate eIF2α, resulting in attenuated rates of translation initiation of most mRNAs and increasing translation of a small group of mRNAs with special 5′ untranslated regions (Hinnebusch, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hinnebusch, 2014.

claim: eIF2α phosphorylation increases translation of a small group of mRNAs with special 5′ untranslated regions that encode potent transcription factors such as ATF4.
source: Diverse stress conditions activate kinases that phosphorylate eIF2α, resulting in attenuated rates of translation initiation of most mRNAs and increasing translation of a small group of mRNAs with special 5′ untranslated regions (Hinnebusch, 2014). The latter encode potent transcription factors such as ATF4 that couple eIF2α phosphorylation to the Integrated Stress Response (ISR) (Harding et al., 2003)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hinnebusch, 2014 and Harding et al., 2003.

claim: Dephosphorylation of eIF2α-P requires the presence of a regulatory subunit, PPP1R15, to direct the catalytic PP1 subunit to its specific substrate.
source: Signalling in the ISR is terminated by eIF2α-P dephosphorylation. This requires the presence of a regulatory subunit, PPP1R15, to direct the catalytic, PP1 subunit, to its specific substrate.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as a known requirement for eIF2α-P dephosphorylation.

claim: Two mammalian genes encode PPP1R15 regulatory subunits: Ppp1r15b (CReP) encoding a constitutively expressed subunit and Ppp1r15a (GADD34) encoding an ISR inducible subunit.
source: Two mammalian genes encode PPP1R15 regulatory subunits. Ppp1r15b (or CReP) encodes a constitutively expressed regulatory subunit (Jousse et al., 2003), whereas Ppp1r15a (or GADD34) encodes an ISR inducible regulatory subunit that contributes to a negative feed-back loop operative in the ISR (Brush et al., 2003; Ma and Hendershot, 2003; Novoa et al., 2001, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published work (Jousse et al., 2003; Brush et al., 2003; Ma and Hendershot, 2003; Novoa et al., 2001, 2003).

claim: A minimal rate of eIF2α-P dephosphorylation is an essential cellular function, as reflected in severe phenotypes of Ppp1r15b mutation or deletion and early lethality of compound Ppp1r15a;b deficient mice.
source: A minimal rate of eIF2α-P dephosphorylation is an essential cellular function, as reflected in the severe phenotypes of Ppp1r15b mutation or deletion and in the very early lethality of compound Ppp1r15a;b deficient mice (Abdulkarim et al., 2015; Harding et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Abdulkarim et al., 2015 and Harding et al., 2009.

claim: Mice lacking PPP1R15A-directed eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (homozygous Ppp1r15atm1Dron) are superficially indistinguishable from wildtype.
source: Interestingly, whilst deletion of the inducible Ppp1r15a gene results in sluggish recovery of protein synthesis during the waning phase of stress (Kojima et al., 2003; Novoa et al., 2003), mice lacking any PPP1R15A-directed eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (homozygous Ppp1r15atm1Dron) are superficially indistinguishable from wildtype.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by citations to Kojima et al., 2003 and Novoa et al., 2003.

claim: Homozygous Ppp1r15atm1Dron mice and cultured cells derived from them are relatively resistant to tunicamycin's lethal effects.
source: Moreover, when challenged with tunicamycin, which causes unfolded protein stress in the endoplasmic reticulum by inhibiting N-linked glycosylation, homozygous Ppp1r15atm1Dron mice and cultured cells derived from them are relatively resistant to the toxin's lethal effects (Marciniak et al., 2004; Reid et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Marciniak et al., 2004 and Reid et al., 2016.

claim: Sustained activity of the ISR in Ppp1r15a mutant mice favours proteostasis by limiting the production of unfolded proteins under stress conditions.
source: This feature is plausibly attributed to sustained activity of the ISR in the Ppp1r15a mutant mice, which favours proteostasis by limiting the production of unfolded proteins under stress conditions (Boyce et al., 2005; Han et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Boyce et al., 2005 and Han et al., 2013.

claim: The neuropathic phenotype associated with Schwann cell expression of mutant P0S63∆ is ameliorated by a concomitant dephosphorylation-defective Ppp1r15atm1Dron mutation.
source: Both the neuropathic phenotype associated with Schwann cell expression of a mutant misfolding-prone myelin constituent, P0S63∆, and a mutant superoxide dismutase expressed in motor neurones are ameliorated by a concomitant dephosphorylation-defective Ppp1r15atm1Dron mutation (D'Antonio et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to D'Antonio et al., 2013 and Wang et al., 2014.

claim: A mutant superoxide dismutase expressed in motor neurones is ameliorated by a concomitant dephosphorylation-defective Ppp1r15atm1Dron mutation.
source: Both the neuropathic phenotype associated with Schwann cell expression of a mutant misfolding-prone myelin constituent, P0S63∆, and a mutant superoxide dismutase expressed in motor neurones are ameliorated by a concomitant dephosphorylation-defective Ppp1r15atm1Dron mutation (D'Antonio et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to D'Antonio et al., 2013 and Wang et al., 2014.

claim: Inflammatory-mediated central nervous system demyelination is ameliorated in Ppp1r15atm1Dron mice.
source: and similar amelioration of inflammatory-mediated central nervous system demyelination is observed in the Ppp1r15atm1Dron mice (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lin et al., 2008.

claim: Salubrinal is a small molecule that increases levels of eIF2α-P and retards its dephosphorylation.
source: Early work led to discovery of salubrinal, a small molecule that increases levels of eIF2α-P and retards its dephosphorylation. However, salubrinal is only known to work in vivo and its mechanism of action remains unclear (Boyce et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Boyce et al., 2005.

claim: Salubrinal only works in vivo and its mechanism of action remains unclear.
source: However, salubrinal is only known to work in vivo and its mechanism of action remains unclear (Boyce et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Boyce et al., 2005.

claim: Guanabenz exerts beneficial effects on proteotoxicity by interfering with eIF2α-P dephosphorylation.
source: but a cell based search for proteostasis regulators suggested that the α2 adrenergic blocker Guanabenz, [(o,o-dichlorobenzylidene)amino]guanidine, might exert its beneficial effects on proteotoxicity by interfering with eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (Tsaytler et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tsaytler et al., 2011.

claim: Sephin1 lost its α2 adrenergic blocking activity but retained its proteostasis promoting properties.
source: This theme was extended further by the discovery of Sephin1, [(o-chlorobenzylidene)amino]guanidine, that had lost its α2 adrenergic blocking activity but retained its proteostasis promoting properties (Das et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Das et al., 2015.

claim: Guanabenz and Sephin1 disrupt the complex between PPP1R15A and PP1.
source: Importantly, biochemical characterization of Guanabenz and Sephin1 suggested that both disrupt the complex between PPP1R15A and PP1, providing strong support for a mechanism of action that involves interfering with PPP1R15A-mediated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (Das et al., 2015), Figure 1C therein).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Das et al., 2015.

claim: A regulatory PPP1R15 subunit is essential for eIF2α-P dephosphorylation in vivo.
source: Genetic analysis reveals that a regulatory PPP1R15 subunit is essential for eIF2α-P dephosphorylation in vivo
evidence: The claim is stated as a result of genetic analysis.

claim: Over-expression of either PPP1R15A or PPP1R15B or merely their conserved C-terminal portion is sufficient to deregulate eIF2α-P dephosphorylation in vivo and inhibit the ISR.
source: and over-expression of either PPP1R15A or PPP1R15B or merely their conserved C-terminal portion, is sufficient to deregulate eIF2α-P dephosphorylation in vivo and inhibit the ISR (Brown et al., 1997; Brush et al., 2003; Jousse et al., 2003; Novoa et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Brown et al., 1997; Brush et al., 2003; Jousse et al., 2003; Novoa et al., 2001.

claim: PPP1R15 regulatory subunits stably bind the catalytic subunit (PP1), but the resulting binary complex is devoid of specificity towards eIF2α-P.
source: Though PPP1R15 regulatory subunits stably bind the catalytic subunit (PP1), the resulting binary complex is devoid of specificity towards eIF2α-P.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as established knowledge.

claim: G-actin joins the PPP1R15-PP1 binary complex as an ancillary subunit to form a ternary complex endowed with substrate-specific eIF2α-P directed phosphatase activity in cells.
source: However, G-actin joins the PPP1R15-PP1 binary complex as an ancillary subunit to form a ternary complex endowed with substrate-specific eIF2α-P directed phosphatase activity, both in cells (Chambers et al., 2015) and when constituted with pure components in vitro (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chambers et al., 2015 and Chen et al., 2015.

claim: G-actin joins the PPP1R15-PP1 binary complex as an ancillary subunit to form a ternary complex endowed with substrate-specific eIF2α-P directed phosphatase activity when constituted with pure components in vitro.
source: However, G-actin joins the PPP1R15-PP1 binary complex as an ancillary subunit to form a ternary complex endowed with substrate-specific eIF2α-P directed phosphatase activity, both in cells (Chambers et al., 2015) and when constituted with pure components in vitro (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chambers et al., 2015 and Chen et al., 2015.

claim: Only the C-terminal 70 residues of PPP1R15A are necessary for substrate-specific dephosphorylation of eIF2α-P.
source: PPP1R15A/GADD34 is a protein of >600 residues, but only the C-terminal 70 residues are necessary for substrate-specific dephosphorylation of eIF2α-P (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The C-terminal active fragment of PPP1R15A is the most conserved segment of the protein, both between homologues of PPP1R15A and with the paralogous PPP1R15B.
source: This active fragment is also the most conserved segment of the protein; both between homologues of PPP1R15A and with the paralogous PPP1R15B (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1B showing sequence alignment.

claim: The C-terminal region of PPP1R15A is natively unfolded, attaining its structure upon binding the PP1 catalytic and the G-actin ancillary subunits.
source: This region of the protein is natively unfolded (Yu et al., 2004), attaining its structure upon binding the PP1 catalytic and the G-actin ancillary subunits (Chen et al., 2015; Choy et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yu et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2015; Choy et al., 2015.

claim: The EC50 of human PPP1R15A for eIF2α-P dephosphorylation is 7 nM.
source: We quantified the dependence of eIF2α-P dephosphorylation rates on both the concentration of the regulatory human PPP1R15A subunit (EC50 = 7 nM) and on the ancillary G-actin subunit (EC50 = 13 nM) (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The EC50 of G-actin for stimulation of eIF2α-P dephosphorylation is 13 nM.
source: We quantified the dependence of eIF2α-P dephosphorylation rates on both the concentration of the regulatory human PPP1R15A subunit (EC50 = 7 nM) and on the ancillary G-actin subunit (EC50 = 13 nM) (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The EC50 of G-actin measured in this study agreed with previous measurements of G-actin's stimulation of enzymatic activity using murine PPP1R15A.
source: The latter values agreed with our previous measurements of G-actin's stimulation of enzymatic activity (in an assay using the murine PPP1R15A) (Chen et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2015.

claim: The EC50 of human PPP1R15A was within an order of magnitude of the affinity of human PPP1R15A for PP1, as measured by isothermal titration calorimetry.
source: whereas the EC50 of human PPP1R15A was within an order of magnitude of the affinity of human PPP1R15A for PP1, as measured by isothermal titration calorimetry (Choy et al., 2015) (see below).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Choy et al., 2015.

claim: The human PPP1R15AV556E mutation abolished all PPP1R15A-mediated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation.
source: The human PPP1R15AV556E mutation alters a key residue, part of the RVxF motif involved in binding of diverse regulatory subunits to PP1 (Egloff et al., 1997); its presence abolished all PPP1R15A-mediated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, with a citation to Egloff et al., 1997.

claim: The human PPP1R15AW582A mutation abolished all PPP1R15A-mediated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation.
source: Two previously-identified mutations in the C-terminal extension of PPP1R15A - the portion that interacts with the G-actin ancillary subunit (human PPP1R15AW582A and PPP1R15AF592A) (Chen et al., 2015) - also abolished all PPP1R15A-mediated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B, with a citation to Chen et al., 2015.

claim: The human PPP1R15AF592A mutation abolished all PPP1R15A-mediated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation.
source: Two previously-identified mutations in the C-terminal extension of PPP1R15A - the portion that interacts with the G-actin ancillary subunit (human PPP1R15AW582A and PPP1R15AF592A) (Chen et al., 2015) - also abolished all PPP1R15A-mediated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, with a citation to Chen et al., 2015.

claim: The human PPP1R15AR578A mutation resulted in a ~4 fold increase in EC50 for eIF2α-P dephosphorylation.
source: A fourth mutation tested affects a residue whose counterpart in human PPP1R15BR658C results in a syndromatic form of diabetes mellitus. Consistent with the destabilizing effect of this mutation on PP1 binding (Abdulkarim et al., 2015), its presence in human PPP1R15AR578A resulted in a ~4 fold increase in EC50 for eIF2α-P dephosphorylation (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, with a citation to Abdulkarim et al., 2015.

claim: At saturating concentrations of human PPP1R15AR578A, eIF2α-P dephosphorylation reactions were three times slower than those assembled with wildtype PPP1R15A.
source: The mutation also affected the maximal stimulation afforded by human PPP1R15AR578A, as even at saturating concentrations of regulatory subunit, eIF2α-P dephosphorylation reactions assembled with the mutant were three times slower than those assembled with the wildtype (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The human PPP1R15AR578A mutation does not have a major effect on the stability of the G-actin containing ternary complex, as the EC50 for G-actin (20 nM) was relatively unaffected.
source: The human PPP1R15AR578A mutation does not appear to have a major effect on the stability of the G-actin containing ternary complex, as the EC50 for G-actin (20 nM) was relatively unaffected (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Biotinylated PPP1R15A533-624 showed a robust 1:1 bimolecular interaction with pure PP1, yielding a koff = 0.21 ± 0.01 min−1 and a Kd = 20 ± 0.61 nM.
source: The biotinylated PPP1R15A533-624 ligand showed a robust 1:1 bimolecular interaction, with pure PP1, yielding a koff = 0.21 ± 0.01 min−1 and a Kd = 20 ± 0.61 nM (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The higher affinity of PPP1R15 for PP1 observed by BLI compared to ITC measurements might reflect the contribution of contacts made by residues C-terminal to PPP1R15AL567.
source: The higher affinity of PPP1R15 for PP1 observed here, compared to isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements of Choy et al. (2015) (Kd = 62 ± 14 nM) might reflect the contribution of contacts made by residues C-terminal to PPP1R15AL567, which are present in the construct used here, but absent from the one used in the ITC measurements (Choy et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is stated as a possible explanation and supported by a citation to Choy et al., 2015.

claim: G-actin binds to the PPP1R15A-PP1 binary complex with a koff = 2.84 ± 0.11 min−1 and Kd = 151 ± 14.3 nM.
source: A robust association-dissociation signal was observed with purified G-actin (koff = 2.84 ± 0.11 min−1 and Kd = 151 ± 14.3 nM) (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The human PPP1R15AV556E mutation abolished all measureable association with PP1, but had no effect on the kinetics of G-actin binding.
source: The human PPP1R15AV556E mutation, affecting the RVxF motif, abolished all measureable association with PP1, but had no effect on the kinetics of G-actin binding. Conversely, the human PPP1R15AF592A mutation markedly enfeebled G-actin binding but had no effect on PP1 binding (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: The human PPP1R15AF592A mutation markedly enfeebled G-actin binding but had no effect on PP1 binding.
source: Conversely, the human PPP1R15AF592A mutation markedly enfeebled G-actin binding but had no effect on PP1 binding (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: PPP1R15A can engage PP1 and G-actin independently, via the N- and C-terminal parts of its active portion.
source: Together, these observations confirm the ability of PPP1R15A to engage PP1 and G-actin independently, via the N- and C-terminal parts of its active portion.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Neither the PPP1R15AR578A nor the PPP1R15AW582A mutations had a major effect on the kinetics of PP1 or G-actin binding.
source: Despite their strong detrimental effects on enzymatic activity (Figures 3C and 4), neither the PPP1R15AR578A nor the PPP1R15AW582A mutations had a major effect on the kinetics of PP1 or G-actin binding (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The tripartite enzymatic assay is sensitive both to mutations that grossly interfere with complex stability (V556E and F592A) and to mutations that more subtly affect the structure of the complex (R578A and W582A).
source: Together, these observations suggest that the tripartite enzymatic assay is sensitive both to mutations that grossly interfere with complex stability (V556E and F592A) and to mutations that more subtly affect the structure of the complex (R578A and W582A).
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Das and colleagues previously reported that addition of 50 µM Sephin1 to tissue culture media disrupts the PPP1R15A-PP1 complex recovered from cells.
source: Das and colleagues previously reported that addition of 50 µM Sephin1 to tissue culture media disrupts the PPP1R15A-PP1 complex recovered from cells (Das et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Das et al., 2015.

claim: Sephin1 at 50 µM had no measureable effect on either the association or dissociation phase of the PPP1R15A-PP1 BLI assay.
source: When added to the BLI assay at a concentration of 50 µM (before exposure to PP1), Sephin1 had no measureable effect on either the association or dissociation phase of the assay (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Sephin1 at 50 µM did not affect the association or dissociation kinetics when biotinylated PP1 was used as the ligand and PPP1R15A533-624 as the analyte.
source: Addition of either the minimal active fragment, human PPP1R15A533-624, or the longer human PPP1R15A325-636, gave rise to a robust BLI signal but addition of Sephin1 affected neither the association nor dissociation phase of the experiment (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Sephin1 at 50 µM did not affect the association or dissociation kinetics when biotinylated PP1 was used as the ligand and PPP1R15A325-636 as the analyte.
source: Addition of either the minimal active fragment, human PPP1R15A533-624, or the longer human PPP1R15A325-636, gave rise to a robust BLI signal but addition of Sephin1 affected neither the association nor dissociation phase of the experiment (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by BLI experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: In the BLI experimental system, 50 µM Sephin1 does not directly interfere with assembly or stability of the PPP1R15A-PP1 complex.
source: However, reproducible inertness in all three assays lends confidence to the conclusion that in this experimental system 50 µM Sephin1 does not directly interfere with assembly or stability of the PPP1R15A-PP1 complex.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion drawn from the BLI experimental observations.

claim: Purified PPP1R15A325-636 added to PP1 and G-actin accelerated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation with an EC50 of 5–10 nM.
source: Addition of purified PPP1R15A325-636 to PP1 and G-actin accelerated eIF2α-P dephosphorylation with an EC50 of 5–10 nM (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Sephin1 had no effect on the in vitro eIF2α-P dephosphorylation reaction assembled with PPP1R15A325-636.
source: However, Sephin1 had no effect on the dephosphorylation reaction (Figure 8B)
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Tautomycin readily inhibited the in vitro eIF2α-P dephosphorylation reaction with an IC50 = 2.4 nM.
source: whilst tautomycin readily inhibited the reaction (IC50 = 2.4 nM) confirming the sensitivity of the assay to a known inhibitor (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Guanabenz at 50 µM proved inert in the in vitro eIF2α-P dephosphorylation assay.
source: The related compound Guanabenz also proved inert, even when added to the enzymatic assay at the high concentration of 50 µM (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Salubrinal at 12 µM had a mild but highly reproducible inhibitory effect on the in vitro eIF2α-P dephosphorylation reaction (inhibition = 22% ± 2.045, p<0.0001, n = 6).
source: Salubrinal, added at 12 µM (higher concentrations led to conspicuous precipitation) had a mild but highly reproducible inhibitory effect (Figure 8E, inhibition = 22% ± 2.045, unpaired t test, p<0.0001, n = 6).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E with statistical analysis.

claim: Sephin1 attenuated the activity of both UPR pathways (ISR and IRE1) in cells exposed to tunicamycin.
source: In keeping with these ideas and with the findings of Das and colleagues (Das et al., 2015), Sephin1 attenuated the activity of both UPR pathways in cells exposed to tunicamycin; an inhibitor of N-linked glycosylation, that promotes misfolding of newly-synthesized proteins (Figure 9A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 9A, with a citation to Das et al., 2015.

claim: Sephin1's effects in the tunicamycin assay were observed only over a narrow concentration range of tunicamycin and at relatively high concentrations of the drug.
source: Though observed only over a narrow concentration range of tunicamycin (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A) and at relatively high concentrations of the drug (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B), Sephin1's effects in this assay can be reconciled with a mechanism involving a net reduction of protein synthesis; as suggested by Das and colleagues.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Sephin1 inhibited induction of the ISR in response to histidinol.
source: Sephin1 also inhibited induction of the ISR in response to histidinol (Figure 9B), an agent that interferes with tRNA charging and thereby activates the eIF2α kinase GCN2 (Zhang et al., 2002) without affecting protein folding.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 9B, with a citation to Zhang et al., 2002.

claim: In the kinase shut-off experiment, eIF2α-P dephosphorylation is normally complete in 60 min in GCN2KO; Ppp1r15bKO CHO-K1 cells.
source: Normally, the dephosphorylation of eIF2α-P is a rapid process, complete in 60 min (Figure 10B, lanes 2–6).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Jasplakinolide markedly delayed eIF2α-P dephosphorylation by depleting the pool of G-actin.
source: It was markedly delayed by inclusion of jasplakinolide (Figure 10B lanes 7–10), which depletes the pool of G-actin (by promoting its oligomerization), thereby depriving the PPP1R15 subunits of an essential co-factor, as observed previously (Chambers et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 10B, with a citation to Chambers et al., 2015.

claim: In GCN2KO; Ppp1r15bKO CHO-K1 cells dependent solely on PPP1R15A, the time-dependent decline of the eIF2α-P signal yielded a time constant of 0.23 min−1 for untreated and 0.19 min−1 for Sephin1 treated samples, an insignificant difference.
source: However, in this experimental system dependent solely on PPP1R15A, the time-dependent decline of the eIF2α-P signal (fitted to an exponential decay curve) yielded a time constant of 0.23 min−1 for the untreated and 0.19 min−1 for the Sephin1 treated sample, an insignificant difference (Figure 10B lanes 11–15, Figure 10—figure supplement 1D and E and Figure 10C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunoblot and quantitative data shown in Figure 10B, Figure 10—figure supplement 1D and E, and Figure 10C.

claim: In tunicamycin-treated GCN2KO; Ppp1r15bKO CHO-K1 cells, eIF2α-P dephosphorylation proceeded rapidly and Sephin1 had no inhibitory effect on the rate of dephosphorylation.
source: eIF2α-P dephosphorylation proceeded rapidly in tunicamycin-treated cells. However, Sephin1 had no inhibitory effect on the rate of dephosphorylation. This experiment reveals that under conditions in which Sephin1 exerts its proteostasis-promoting activities, it does not affect rates of eIF2a-P dephosphorylation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Sephin1 retained its ability to attenuate the response of both the XBP1s::Turquoise and the CHOP::GFP reporter in tunicamycin treated PPP1R15A null cells.
source: Sephin1 retained its ability to attenuate the response of both the XBP1s::Turquoise and the CHOP::GFP reporter in tunicamycin treated PPP1R15A null cells (Figure 11B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 11B.

claim: Sephin1 retained its ability to attenuate the response of both reporters in histidinol-treated PPP1R15A null cells.
source: Similar observations were made in regard to the effect of Sephin1 in histidinol-treated cells (Figure 11C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 11C.

claim: Sephin1 exerts its proteostatic effect(s) in cells lacking PPP1R15A.
source: These observations suggest that Sephin1 also exerts its proteostatic effect(s) in cells lacking PPP1R15A.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations in PPP1R15A null cells.

claim: Sephin1 retained its ability to attenuate the XBP1s::Turquoise reporter in tunicamycin-treated eIF2αS51A mutant cells.
source: Surprisingly, Sephin1 retained its ability to attenuate the XBP1s::Turquoise reporter in tunicamycin-treated eIF2αS51Amutant cells (Figure 12C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 12C.

claim: Activity of the CHOP::GFP reporter was strongly attenuated in mutant eIF2αS51A cells.
source: As CHOP activation is highly dependent on the ISR (Harding et al., 2000), activity of the CHOP::GFP reporter was strongly attenuated in mutant eIF2αS51Acells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Harding et al., 2000.

claim: Residual activation of the CHOP::GFP reporter by tunicamycin in eIF2αS51A cells was attenuated by Sephin1.
